candidates.title: Reproductive optimization as future demographic driver
candidates.shift: Emerging embryo/genetic optimization discourse could eventually reshape population composition, labor pools, and consumer demographics decades out.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, off-map from architecture but could feed the demographic branch — who staffs and shops future stores. Strange because retail foresight almost never touches germline tech.
candidates.evidence: Noema Magazine essay 'Optimized Offspring' surveys emerging embryo-selection/optimization discourse; no dataset cited, conceptual piece.
candidates.initial_analysis: This is an example of a civilizational-scale demographic shift moving from speculative to discussed; if it accelerates, future labor and consumer pools could shift composition in ways that ripple into staffing and store demand decades out.
candidates.author: Brigida D'Agostino

candidates.title: AI-plotted multi-generational mission as long-horizon planning template
candidates.shift: A nonprofit's AI-designed 80,000-year interstellar trajectory shows AI now handling planning horizons vastly beyond any built-asset lifecycle.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, off-map (space) — but models extreme long-horizon infrastructure planning; could inform how foresight teams frame multi-generational real-estate or asset decisions.
candidates.evidence: MIT Technology Review reports Fermi Explorer Mission's AI-plotted trajectory to Alpha Centauri, targeting launch by end of 2029.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of AI moving from optimizing short operational tasks to planning across timescales no human institution has managed; if normalized, similar tools could reshape how long-lived physical assets are planned and valued.
candidates.author: Michelle Kim

candidates.title: Film-set architecture as informal place-making standard
candidates.shift: Indian cinema constructs elaborate, never-built architectural fantasies (courtyards, palaces, streets) that persist in public imagination and shape real-world place expectations after sets are dismantled.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: retail/experience designers may borrow this 'phantom architecture' logic for store environments. Strange because it's architecture that never physically endures yet still shapes real expectations of place.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily feature on Indian film sets constructing full courtyards, palaces, and neighborhoods that shape public place-imagination for millions of viewers.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of media-generated 'unreal' architecture setting real expectations for place and experience; if retail experience design absorbs this logic, stores could increasingly be designed as cinematic sets rather than functional buildings.
candidates.author: Ananya Nayak

candidates.title: Micro-retail embedded inside public park infrastructure
candidates.shift: A florist kiosk is built directly into a major Beijing public park, blurring the line between civic green infrastructure and standalone retail real estate.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative — signals a format where small retail is inserted into public infrastructure rather than occupying separate real estate; peripheral geography (Beijing) possibly setting a small-format-in-park precedent.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily profile of West Garden Florist by LUO studio, sited within Haidian Park, Beijing, amid parks evolving toward human-centered use.
candidates.initial_analysis: This is an example of retail decoupling from dedicated commercial real estate and instead nesting inside shared public infrastructure; if it spreads, store-siting logic could shift from leased retail footprint to negotiated public-space concessions.
candidates.author: Valeria Silva
